**Unofficial** integration, not affiliated with GCE Electronics. It reads an
**Eco-Devices** (the DIN-rail teleinformation module, **not the Eco-Devices
RT2**, which has another API) through its **local JSON API**, no cloud.
**Read-only**: it only sends read requests, the Eco-Devices receives no
command.

**Never tested with a real Eco-Devices**: built from the GCE Electronics
documentation (wiki, "API JSON" section) and the pyecodevices and ecodevices
(Home Assistant) projects.

## What you get

One device per input in use:

- **Teleinfo 1** and **Teleinfo 2** (an electricity meter in **historic**
  mode on the input: a Linky in historic mode or an electronic meter):
  - **Apparent power** (VA): the PAPP value of the meter, read every 15
    seconds; the energy contracts of Gladys compare it with your subscribed
    power;
  - **Consumption index** (kWh): the sum of the indexes of the tariff option
    of the meter (base; off-peak + peak; EJP; the six Tempo indexes), sent
    once a minute; the Gladys energy monitoring turns it into consumption and
    cost;
  - each **tariff index** (kWh) as a plain sensor, for information (never
    counted in the energy monitoring).
- **Counter 1** and **Counter 2** (the pulse inputs), only when you set them
  to **water** or **gas** in the configuration:
  - **Index** (m³): the total index of the meter;
  - **Consumption today** (m³): reset every day by the Eco-Devices, at the
    hour set in its configuration page.

Water and gas do not go through the Gladys energy monitoring (they are
volumes, not kWh).

This is **not** the `gladys-teleinfo` integration (a LiXee USB key): if your
meter is already read by another integration, keep only one, or the
consumption would be counted twice. Likewise, if Teleinfo 2 is a sub-meter of
Teleinfo 1, put it under the main meter in the Gladys energy monitoring.

## Setup

1. Find the IP address of the Eco-Devices (in your router or with GCE
   ScanDevice) and preferably give it a fixed address.
2. Check that the JSON API answers: open
   `http://<address>/api/xdevices.json?cmd=10` in a browser; you should see
   an answer starting with `{"product":"Eco-devices"`. Otherwise, update the
   firmware of the Eco-Devices.
3. In Gladys, install the integration and fill in:
   - **Eco-Devices address** (with a port only if it is not 80);
   - **User name** and **password**, only if the secure access of the
     Eco-Devices is on (System tab, Security block). The password is kept by
     Gladys in its database, never shown again, never logged, sent only to
     the Eco-Devices address (HTTP Basic authentication in plain HTTP on your
     network: what the Eco-Devices offers). A password without a user name is
     refused;
   - for each **pulse counter**: water, gas or "not used", and the **unit of
     its index** on the Eco-Devices (litres by default, the most common
     setting: 1 pulse = 1 litre; otherwise cubic metres). Compare the index
     Gladys shows with the one of the meter itself. Choose them **before**
     creating the device: changing the unit later makes the index jump or
     drop (see below).
4. Save, then create the devices from the **Discover** tab.

The **Test the connection** button reads the Eco-Devices once when a read is
due (never more than one every 15 seconds), otherwise tells the last read.

## Index guard

The energy monitoring counts every rise of an index in full. So that a wrong
index (a meter replaced, a read error) is held instead of billed:

- an index at 0 is never sent;
- a rise larger than what the home can consume since the last value (100 kW
  for electricity, 10 m³/h for water, 16 m³/h for gas) is a **jump**; a value
  lower than the last one is a **drop**;
- a jump or a drop is **held**: the last accepted value is sent again, the
  status of the integration shows it, and it is kept in `/data` across
  restarts. Neither time nor repetition confirms it;
- **a right jump** (and, for a water or gas counter, **a right drop**, for
  example after correcting the index entered in the Eco-Devices) is taken in
  **two clicks** on "Accept the held index": the first click lists the held
  values and takes nothing; the second, a few seconds to 5 minutes later,
  takes the values listed (plus what the meter may measure meanwhile), only
  if they did not change otherwise. Saving the configuration accepts nothing.
  The badge of the device turns orange while an index is held;
- changing the **unit** of a pulse counter in the configuration (litres or
  m³) converts the reference value: neither a jump nor a drop;
- **a drop of a teleinfo consumption index is never accepted** (it is a sum
  of indexes: it only drops when it is another meter). It happens when the
  meter is **replaced**, or when the **tariff option changes** (base to
  off-peak or Tempo, for example) and the meter starts its new indexes from
  zero. The status of the integration says so ("Consumption index DROP held,
  never accepted"). The only way out is to **delete the device** of that
  input and **create it again** from the Discover tab. What it costs:
  - the whole history of the device is lost: index, power, and the
    **consumption and cost** computed by the energy monitoring;
  - it must be placed again in the energy tree and tied to your contract;
  - Gladys refuses to delete a device with more than 5000 states (about 21
    hours of power at one value every 15 seconds): it purges them in the
    background, try again later.
    Keeping the history without accepting the drop (a new device created
    beside the old one) is not possible in this version;
- for an electricity index with several tariffs, the total is built only
  when every index of the option is read; a tariff index back to 0 or
  dropping alone is a read error: no index that time.

## How it works

- One read every 15 seconds (`cmd=10`), never more often, even after a
  restart, a save of the configuration, a click or a reconnection (the time
  of the last read is kept in `/data`).
- The consumption of the day (`cmd=20`) is read every 5 minutes, only when a
  pulse counter is set; if it fails, the indexes go on and it is tried again
  after 5 minutes, then 10, up to 1 hour.
- One request at a time to the Eco-Devices.
- If the Eco-Devices does not answer: new try after 15 s, then doubled, up
  to 10 minutes. If it answers 429 or 5xx: a pause of 1 minute to 6 hours,
  kept across restarts.
- **Login refused** (401/403 on the page of the indexes): the reads stop,
  even after a restart, until you change the address, the user name or the
  password, or the "Test the connection" button succeeds. A refusal on the
  page of the day does not count as a refused login.
- If the power and every index of a teleinfo input stay the same for 15
  minutes (teleinfo cable out?), the power is no longer sent.
- If the configuration cannot be read from Gladys at a connection, it is
  asked again after 5 s, then doubled, up to 5 minutes, without end.
- If the state file in `/data` cannot be read (or written), no index is sent
  until it can (a held value may be in it); the power goes on. A file that
  cannot be read is not overwritten. If it is damaged (after a power cut, for
  example), delete the file `ecodevices-state.json` from the `/data` volume of
  the integration (on the Docker host of Gladys) and restart the integration:
  it starts from an empty state (the held indexes are forgotten).

## Limits

- Eco-Devices RT2 not supported (another API).
- The **standard** teleinfo mode of the Linky is not read: switch the meter
  to historic mode (ask your supplier) or use another module.
- Pulse counters are read as water or gas only (no electricity pulses).
- The Tempo colour of today and tomorrow is not published.

## Troubleshooting

If the status says the answer gives no index of some keys ("the answer gives
no HCHP", for example), send the developer the `cmd=10` answer below: the
names of the off-peak and EJP indexes are inferred, not yet confirmed on a
real Eco-Devices.

On the same network as the Eco-Devices:

```bash
curl -s "http://192.168.1.20/api/xdevices.json?cmd=10"; echo
curl -s "http://192.168.1.20/api/xdevices.json?cmd=20"; echo
## with the secure access:
curl -s -u admin "http://192.168.1.20/api/xdevices.json?cmd=10"; echo
```

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Eco-Devices asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GCE Eco-Devices | `section` | No | Unofficial connector, not affiliated with GCE Electronics. It reads an Eco-Devices (not the RT2) through its local JSON API, without any cloud: for each teleinformation input with a meter in historic mode (Linky or electronic meter), its apparent power and its consumption index (the sum of its tariff indexes: base, off-peak/peak, EJP or Tempo) for the Gladys energy monitoring, and each tariff index as a plain sensor; for each pulse counter set below (water or gas), its index and its consumption of the day in m³. Read-only. Not the gladys-teleinfo integration (a LiXee USB key): use one of them per meter, never both. Never tested with a real Eco-Devices. |
| Eco-Devices address | `string` | Yes | The IP address of the Eco-Devices on your network (shown by your router or by GCE ScanDevice), with a port only if it is not 80. Preferably give it a fixed address; if it changes, enter the new one: each input keeps its device and history. |
| User name (optional) | `string` | No | Only if the secure access of the Eco-Devices is on (System tab, Security block): its user name. Leave empty otherwise. |
| Password (optional) | `secret` | No | The password of that login. Kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again, never logged, sent only to the Eco-Devices address above (HTTP Basic authentication in plain HTTP on your network: the Eco-Devices offers nothing else). If the Eco-Devices refuses it, reads stop until you change it or click "Test the connection". |
| Pulse counter 1 | `select` | No | What the meter wired on pulse input C1 of the Eco-Devices measures. "Not used" leaves it out. Choose before creating its device. |
| Unit of the index of counter 1 | `select` | No | The unit of the index the Eco-Devices shows for counter 1 (litres by default, as most setups use: 1 pulse = 1 litre). Compare it with the index of the meter itself. Gladys shows m³. |
| Pulse counter 2 | `select` | No | What the meter wired on pulse input C2 of the Eco-Devices measures. "Not used" leaves it out. Choose before creating its device. |
| Unit of the index of counter 2 | `select` | No | The unit of the index the Eco-Devices shows for counter 2 (litres by default, as most setups use: 1 pulse = 1 litre). Compare it with the index of the meter itself. Gladys shows m³. |

## How to install Eco-Devices in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Eco-Devices appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-ecodevices:0.1.1`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-ecodevices](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-ecodevices).

Eco-Devices requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Eco-Devices is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7), not by the Gladys core team.
